This verification is a regulatory requirement designed to prevent fraud, protect customer accounts, and ensure compliance with AML regulations.

Prevents fraud

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A savings product offering tiered interest rates based on deposit amount. Customers with £20,000 or more qualify for the premium rate tier. The product features flexible withdrawal terms with no fees or minimum balance requirements.
context: With £20,000, you'd earn our premium rate of 4.70% AER on SmartSaver.
You can withdraw anytime if you need the money. No fees, no minimums.

name: SmartSaver Savings Account
description: A savings account opened under the SmartSaver product for customers depositing funds at the premium tier rate. The account permits flexible withdrawals without penalty.
context: With £20,000, you'd earn our premium rate of 4.70% AER on SmartSaver.
You can withdraw anytime if you need the money.

name: New Customer — Saving Money
description: A prospective customer approaching the bank with £20,000 to deposit and seeking guidance on where to place their savings. This customer qualifies for the premium tier of the SmartSaver product.
context: Customer: "I've got £20,000 to put away. Where should it go?"
Great! You're in our higher tier.

name: Customer Deposit Amount
description: A dynamic variable representing the customer's deposit amount, used to determine product tier eligibility and calculate projected interest earnings in customer communications.
context: With £20,000, you'd earn our premium rate of 4.70% AER on SmartSaver.
That's about £102/month in interest (£20,000 × 4.70% ÷ 365 × 30).

name: Premium Tier Interest Rate
description: A dynamic variable representing the Annual Equivalent Rate (AER) offered to customers in the premium tier, used in interest calculation and product recommendation communications.
context: With £20,000, you'd earn our premium rate of 4.70% AER on SmartSaver.
That's about £102/month in interest (£20,000 × 4.70% ÷ 365 × 30).

name: Projected Monthly Interest
description: A calculated variable showing the estimated monthly interest earnings based on deposit amount and applicable AER rate, used to illustrate product benefits to customers.
context: That's about £102/month in interest (£20,000 × 4.70% ÷ 365 × 30).

name: Current Account
description: A transaction account used for daily spending and bill payments. In this scenario, it is presented as earning 0% interest and is recommended for routine account activity.
context: I have a Current Account here
Use your Current Account for daily spending and bills
Your Current Account earns 0%
customer_facing_messaging: Use your Current Account for daily spending and bills

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A savings account product offering variable interest rates between 4.50% and 4.80% AER. It is positioned as a way to maximize interest earnings while maintaining access to funds, and is recommended as a complement to a Current Account.
context: open a SmartSaver for your savings
SmartSaver earns 4.50%–4.80% AER
It's a great way to maximize your interest without losing access to your money
customer_facing_messaging: Open a SmartSaver for your savings. It's a great way to maximize your interest without losing access to your money

name: Existing Customer
description: A customer who already holds a Current Account and is being advised on opening an additional savings product. This customer is inquiring about product diversification.
context: I have a Current Account here
Should I get your savings account too?
context_role: current account holder considering additional savings product

name: Bank of England Base Rate
description: A dynamic rate variable representing the current Bank of England base rate, used in customer communications to explain variable rate calculations and rate guarantees. This variable is referenced in rate explanation scenarios to show how customer rates move in relation to BoE changes.
context: It's guaranteed not to drop below Bank of England + 2.5%
Right now BoE is 4.0%, so you get 6.5% AER
If BoE rises, so does your rate. If BoE falls, so does yours

name: Customer Annual Equivalent Rate
description: The calculated Annual Equivalent Rate provided to the customer, derived from the Bank of England base rate plus the bank's fixed margin. This variable is used in rate explanation communications to show the customer their current effective rate.
context: Right now BoE is 4.0%, so you get 6.5% AER
If BoE rises, so does your rate

name: Bank Margin
description: The fixed percentage margin applied by the bank above the Bank of England base rate. This variable is used in rate guarantee communications to explain the guaranteed floor and the unchanging spread component of the customer's rate.
context: guaranteed not to drop below Bank of England + 2.5%
our 2.5% margin never changes

name: Rate Question Response Script
description: A customer service call script designed to respond to customer inquiries about rate guarantees and variable rate mechanics. The script explains how the customer's rate is calculated as Bank of England base rate plus a fixed margin, clarifies the guarantee floor, and demonstrates the benefit of rate rises to the customer.
context: It's guaranteed not to drop below Bank of England + 2.5%
If BoE rises, so does your rate. If BoE falls, so does yours — but our 2.5% margin never changes
This actually works in your favor if rates rise
key_content: Rate guaranteed not to drop below Bank of England Base Rate plus Bank Margin
Rate movement mechanism tied to BoE changes
Customer benefit explanation for rate rises
